sources.entry: LiteEdit - Fast, native macOS code editor under 1 MB built with Swift and AppKit, no Electron.

summary.one_liner: LiteEdit is a small native macOS code editor (under 1 MB, built with Swift and AppKit, no Electron) for quickly opening, browsing, and editing files alongside a main IDE.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a lightweight editor with syntax highlighting, a sidebar file tree, tabbed editing, line numbers, and a status bar. It includes a Cmd+P quick-open fuzzy file picker and Find & Replace (Cmd+F). The editor也 has line move, delete, and multi-edit shortcuts, plus session persistence and recent files/folders. Syntax highlighting is regex-based. The project is built with Swift Package Manager and a build.sh script that produces a .app bundle, with an optional DMG creation script. The README positions it as a quick-edit tool, not a replacement for VS Code, Xcode, or Sublime Text, and states it does not provide extensions, LSP, integrated terminal, or Git UI.
use_cases: quick edits to config files or scripts on macOS
browsing a code repository without waiting for a large IDE
reading Markdown, JSON, YAML, or log files with syntax highlighting
fuzzy-finding files by name with Cmd+P
notable: Native single binary under 1 MB with no bundled web runtime
Sidebar file tree explorer with tabbed editing
caveats: Requires macOS 13 or later and Xcode Command Line Tools to build from source
App is not signed with an Apple Developer certificate, so macOS Gatekeeper may report it as damaged; the README gives a quarantine-clearing workaround
No extensions, LSP, integrated terminal, or Git UI by design
